sourceNote: Records curated from Wikipedia articles and publicly documented sources. Original 6 stubs were from Wikipedia Geosearch API; sourceRecordIds preserved where available. Rishikesh destination center: 30.10833, 78.29722. Rajaji NP coordinate (30.058, 78.173) is ~15km west of city; entry and safaris are booked from Rishikesh. All records needs_review.

places.name: Lakshman Jhula
places.description: Iconic iron suspension bridge (239m) over the Ganges, built in 1939. The original bridge was permanently closed to pedestrians in 2019 due to structural concerns; a new replacement bridge (Lakshman Setu) was under construction. The Lakshman Jhula area itself — the dense cluster of ashrams, shops, cafes, and multi-storey temples on both banks — remains one of Rishikesh's liveliest neighbourhoods. The eastern Tapovan bank and the Garhwal-side market are worth exploring on foot.
places.openingDays: Area open all day; original bridge access restricted

places.name: Ram Jhula
places.description: Suspension footbridge (450m) over the Ganges connecting Swarg Ashram on the east bank to Shivananda Nagar on the west, built 1986. Wider and newer than the original Lakshman Jhula; remains open to pedestrians. The bridge is a principal crossing point between the ashram belt and the road network. The famous 13-storey Tera Manzil Temple is adjacent on the east bank. A lively crossing day and night with constant foot traffic, pilgrims, and sadhus.

places.name: Parmarth Niketan
places.description: Largest ashram in Rishikesh, founded 1942, set on the eastern bank of the Ganges near Ram Jhula. Runs yoga, meditation, and spiritual education programmes. The ashram's daily Ganga Aarti at sunset (approximately 18:00–18:30, seasonally adjusted) on the ghats is the most-attended ceremony in Rishikesh — hundreds of candles and lamps are offered to the river. Open to visitors; the ghat is free. Longer residential programmes and yoga retreats are paid.

places.name: Beatles Ashram
places.description: Former ashram of Maharishi Mahesh Yogi (Chaurasi Kutia), where The Beatles and other celebrities stayed in 1968 to study Transcendental Meditation. Abandoned in 1981 and reclaimed by forest; now open as a heritage site managed by the Forest Department. The campus has meditation domes, Beatles-themed murals painted by visiting artists, and overgrown but striking stone structures returning to jungle. Entry fee applies (charged by Forest Dept). Open daily; photography permitted. A 2km walk from Ram Jhula.

places.name: Nilkanth Mahadev Temple
places.description: Important Shiva temple at 1675m altitude in the Pauri Garhwal hills, 32km by road from Rishikesh. Marks the site where Shiva is said to have consumed the Halahala poison that emerged from the churning of the cosmic ocean (the story of Nilkanth — blue-throated). The main temple houses a Shiva Linga with natural spring water. The approach passes through forest and offers views of the Ganges valley. Shared taxis from Rishikesh. Best visited on weekdays to avoid crowds.

places.name: Rajaji National Park
places.description: Nationally protected forest spanning the Shivalik range across Haridwar, Rishikesh, and Dehradun districts — 820 sq km in total. Holds one of the most accessible elephant populations in northern India along with tigers, leopards, cheetal, and over 300 bird species. The Chilla range (accessible from Haridwar) and the Motichur range (Rishikesh side) both run jeep safaris. Season: Nov 15 – Jun 15; park closed monsoon. Entry and safari permits from the Range Officer.
places.area: Shivalik Range; entry via Rishikesh or Haridwar

places.name: Triveni Ghat
places.description: Main public ghat in Rishikesh town at the confluence of three rivers — Ganges, Yamuna, and the mythical Saraswati. The most accessible ghat from the town centre. Evening Ganga Aarti performed by priests at sunset daily, smaller in scale than Parmarth Niketan's but more spontaneous. Morning ritual bathing is common; the ghat is active from before dawn. Boats available for hire for short Ganges rides. Free to visit; boats charged separately.
places.openingDays: Open all day; Aarti at sunset

places.name: White-water Rafting, Rishikesh
places.description: Rishikesh is the white-water rafting capital of India; the Ganges through the Shivaliks provides Grade II–IV rapids depending on the stretch. Main run options: Shivpuri to Rishikesh (12km, ~2h, Grade II–III, accessible for beginners), Brahmapuri to Rishikesh (9km), or the longer Marine Drive to Rishikesh (26km, 2 days). Season: Sep–Oct (post-monsoon high water) and Mar–May (pre-monsoon). Dozens of licensed operators in Rishikesh; all provide rafts, helmets, and life jackets. Coordinate is Shivpuri camp area — the most popular starting point.
places.openingDays: Sep–Oct and Mar–May (main seasons); some operators run Nov–Feb

places.name: Tera Manzil Temple
places.description: Striking 13-storey pink temple on the Ganges bank adjacent to Ram Jhula, housing shrines to multiple Hindu deities (Triyambakeshwar Shiva, Vishnu, Durga, Hanuman, Ganesha and others) across its floors. The terrace on the upper floors provides panoramic views of the Ganges, Ram Jhula bridge, and the Shivalik hills. One of the most visually distinctive buildings in Rishikesh. Free to enter; open to visitors through the day.

places.name: Neer Garh Waterfall
places.description: Two-tiered waterfall in a forested ravine, accessible via a 2km trail from the Lakshman Jhula area. The path follows a stream through dense forest; the lower fall is a popular swimming spot. Much quieter than the Ganges ghats; offers a short nature break without leaving Rishikesh. Small entry fee charged at the gate. Best visited outside peak monsoon when the trail is not flooded. Combine with Lakshman Jhula area in the same half-day.
places.area: Forest above Lakshman Jhula, 9km from Rishikesh
places.openingDays: Daily 07:00–17:00 (may be restricted in heavy monsoon)

places.name: Kunjapuri Devi Temple
places.description: Shakti temple at 1676m altitude, 25km from Rishikesh by road. One of the Siddha Peethas (sacred sites associated with Sati). The temple is reached via a 1.5km hill climb from the motorable road; the top offers one of the finest sunrise panoramas in the Garhwal region, with views of the Himalayas including Bandarpunch, Swargarohini and Gangotri groups. Best visited pre-dawn for sunrise; most visitors hire a vehicle from Rishikesh. Free entry to temple.

places.name: Swarg Ashram
places.description: The main ashram belt on the east (Garhwal) bank of the Ganges, stretching between Ram Jhula and Lakshman Jhula. Named after the Kali Kamliwala Ashram and the general spiritual character of the neighbourhood. The strip contains dozens of ashrams, dharamshalas, yoga schools, and vegetarian cafes — no alcohol or non-vegetarian food is sold in the area. Walking the ghats and lanes between the two bridges at dusk is the classic Rishikesh experience. Free to walk and visit the public ghats.
places.area: East bank, between Ram Jhula and Lakshman Jhula

places.name: Rishikesh Café Culture — Lakshman Jhula
places.description: The Lakshman Jhula neighbourhood is lined with rooftop cafés offering views of the Ganga and Himalayas. Serving yoga-retreat food — hummus wraps, banana pancakes, avocado toast, and fresh ginger lemon tea. Popular with international travellers and sadhus alike.

places.name: Rishikesh Evening Aarti Prasad
places.description: After the Parmarth Niketan Ganga Aarti, local vendors offer prasad sweets and flower offerings. Street food near Ram Jhula and Triveni Ghat includes puri bhaji, samosa, and chai — best consumed while watching the post-aarti gathering.
